# Investment Committee Memo — Molarity Health, Inc. (Series B)

**To:** Investment Committee | **From:** VP, Stonebridge Growth Partners | **Deal lead:** Richard Miles
**Ask:** $15.0M Series B Preferred | **Status:** Term sheet received, pre-signing

---

## 1. Recommendation

**Invest with conditions — do not approve as currently structured.** Molarity has a product customers value and a real market, but three things in the materials don't survive restatement: (i) at $60M pre / $75M post we own **20%, not 25%**; (ii) gross margin is **~74%, not 81%**, once production hosting is put back in cost of revenue, and it is flat-to-declining, not improving; (iii) growth has decelerated (~60% → ~38%), NRR has fallen to 103%, and the 18% customer has told us it may build its own platform in 2026. I recommend we approve up to $15M **only if**: (a) we counter at **$45M pre / $60M post (25%)** with a walk-away at $65M post; (b) BrightSmile's renewal is resolved before close or the price is set on ex-BrightSmile ARR; and (c) management delivers restated financials and agrees to monthly cohort reporting. With 10 months of cash and (to confirm) no competing term sheet, we have the leverage to get this.

## 2. Company and thesis

- Cloud practice-management software (scheduling, insurance verification, billing) for US dental practices; $14.0M ARR, displacing on-prem incumbents (Dentrix/Eaglesoft) in independents and small groups.
- Product ROI is tangible — one owner reports two front-desk hours saved per day — which supports pricing power and module expansion (payments, patient comms, RCM) if execution on support holds.
- Thesis: vertical SaaS with sticky workflows in a fragmented, under-digitized market, acquirable by distributors (Schein, Patterson) or PE-backed dental platforms at 5–6x ARR.

## 3. Key metrics (restated where we disagree; $M)

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | LTM Sep-25 | Formula / note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARR (period end) | 7.0 | 11.2 | 14.0 | Mgmt |
| ARR growth | — | 60% | ~38% (est.) | 11.2/7.0−1; Sep-24 ARR interpolated ≈10.2 → 14.0/10.2−1 |
| Revenue | 6.0 | 10.5 | 13.2 | Mgmt |
| Reported gross margin | 76.7% | 81.0% | 81.1% | (Rev − CoR)/Rev |
| Production hosting in R&D | — | 0.77 | 0.94 | 85% × AWS ($0.9; $1.1) per engineering |
| **Restated CoR** | 1.4 | 2.77 | 3.44 | Reported CoR + production hosting |
| **Restated gross margin** | 76.7% | **73.7%** | **74.0%** | (10.5−2.77)/10.5; (13.2−3.44)/13.2 |
| Net burn | 6.1 | 9.0 | 9.6 | Mgmt |
| Net new ARR | — | 4.2 | ~3.8 (est.) | ΔARR over 12 months |
| **Burn multiple** | — | 2.1x | **~2.5x** | Net burn / net new ARR |
| NRR (TTM, by cohort year) | 124% (’22) | 112% (’23) | **103% (’24)** | Mgmt |
| Implied gross retention | — | — | ~91% | 1 − 9% logo churn (dollar GRR to confirm) |
| Implied net expansion | 33 pts | 21 pts | 12 pts | NRR − GRR |
| Largest customer | — | — | 18% = $2.5M | 0.18 × 14.0 |
| Runway | — | — | 10 months | 8.0 cash / 0.8 monthly burn → ~Jul-2026 |

**Takeaways:** FY2023 had hosting in CoR, so the "like-for-like" GM trend is 76.7% → 73.7% → 74.0% — the reclassification manufactured the improvement story. Expansion revenue has largely disappeared; growth is now almost entirely new logos, bought at a worsening burn multiple.

## 4. Valuation and terms

| Item | Term sheet | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Pre / post-money | $60.0M / $75.0M | Post = 60 + 15 |
| **Stonebridge ownership** | **20.0%** | 15 / 75. Richard's "25%" implies $45M pre |
| Option pool (in pre) | 10% of post = $7.5M | Existing pool 3% of pre FD ≈ 2.2% of post |
| Pool top-up | ≈ 7.8% of post ≈ **$5.9M** | 10% − 2.2%; dilutes existing holders only |
| **Effective pre-money** | **$54.1M** | 60.0 − 5.9 |
| Post / ARR | 5.4x | 75 / 14.0 |
| Post / ARR ex-BrightSmile | 6.5x | 75 / 11.5 |
| Liquidation preference | 1x non-participating | Acceptable; confirm seniority vs. Series A |
| Governance | 1 board seat | Add pro rata, information rights, protective provisions |

**Assessment.** 5.4x ARR for ~38% growth, 74% GM, 103% NRR and a 2.5x burn multiple is full but not absurd — *if* BrightSmile stays. It does not price the disclosed build-vs-buy risk.

**Proposed counter:** $15M at **$45M pre / $60M post**, pool 10% of post inside the pre → **25.0%**, 4.3x ARR (effective pre ≈ $40M). **Walk-away:** $65M post → 23.1%, 4.6x ARR. Alternative if management holds price: $10M at close + $5M tranche on BrightSmile multi-year renewal, or a conversion-price adjustment if BrightSmile gives notice within 12 months.

## 5. Key risks and mitigants

1. **BrightSmile concentration ($2.5M, 18%).** COO has hired a CTO and is evaluating an in-house build in 2026. Loss takes ARR to $11.5M and 2024 NRR to ~85%. *Mitigant:* renewal as closing condition, or price/ratchet on ex-BrightSmile ARR; meet the CTO directly.
2. **Retention decay.** NRR 124% → 103%; 9% logo churn; a 12-office group says support "has slipped." *Mitigant:* use-of-proceeds earmark for customer success; monthly cohort/CSAT reporting covenant; verify dollar GRR.
3. **Reporting quality.** Hosting reclassification overstated GM by ~7 points. *Mitigant:* restated financials pre-close; audit; finance leadership hire within 6 months.
4. **Capital efficiency / financing risk.** Burn multiple 2.5x and worsening; 10 months cash. $15M buys ~29 months at current burn, but a Series C in 2027 requires burn multiple <1.5x. *Mitigant:* board-approved plan with efficiency milestones.
5. **Market structure.** DSO consolidation shrinks the independent base, and DSOs standardize on enterprise vendors (Denticon) or build. *Mitigant:* thesis must rest on independents/small groups; underwrite DSO revenue conservatively.
6. **Ownership shortfall.** 20% vs. 25% in our model materially changes return math (≈$225M exit for 3x gross at 20%, before Series C dilution). *Mitigant:* counter above.

## 6. Diligence items to close before signing

- Customer-level ARR file; NRR and dollar GRR by segment (independent / group / DSO) and ex-BrightSmile; churn reasons for the 9%.
- BrightSmile contract (term, renewal date, termination rights, pricing); call with new CTO.
- AWS invoices by environment to confirm the 85% split; restated P&L; ARR definition (contracted vs. live, implementation fees).
- Support metrics by quarter: ticket volume, time-to-resolve, CSAT; CS headcount per $1M ARR.
- Pipeline, new-logo CAC and payback; sales capacity and quota attainment.
- Full cap table, prior preference stack, vesting, hiring plan justifying a 10% pool; confirm 3% unallocated.
- 13-week cash forecast; deferred revenue, AP aging; confirm no competing term sheet.
- HIPAA/SOC 2 status, uptime history; 5+ additional references including 2 churned customers.

## 7. What we'd need to believe

- Molarity sustains ~35% ARR growth in independents and small groups while NRR recovers to 110%+ through module attach — the product ROI is real enough to support this.
- BrightSmile either renews or its loss is absorbed by $3.5–4M/yr of new-logo ARR without derailing the growth narrative.
- Restated ~74% GM can reach 78–80% through hosting optimization and pricing; otherwise the terminal multiple is capped at ~4–5x.
- Burn multiple improves below 1.5x by 2027, so the Series C is raised from strength.
- Exit path: ~$50M ARR by 2029–30 at 5–6x → $250–300M, delivering 3–4x to us at 23–25% entry ownership net of one more round.

**Bottom line:** Good product, honest-to-fair price if restructured, but the deal lead's headline ownership and management's margin story are both wrong. Approve the counter; pass if BrightSmile is unresolved and price stays above $65M post.
